judgment.rationale: B6.2.3.1 (Strand 2 Algebra / Sub-Strand 3 Variables and Equations) asks pupils to solve single-variable one-step equations with whole number coefficients, while B6.1.2.2 (Strand 1 Number / Sub-Strand 2 Number Operations) asks for understanding of multiplication of 2- or 3-digit numbers by 2- or 3-digit numbers. There is genuine conceptual coherence: whole-number multiplicative operations are the operational content used and reinforced when solving one-step equations with whole number coefficients, so the two reinforce one another across strands. However, both sit at the same configured coordinate (Grade BASIC 6, rank 2) in different strands, and the evidence supplied (shared 'number' token, weak code-prefix and rank-proximity signals, no Learning Components for either endpoint) does not substantively establish that multi-digit multiplication algorithm work is developmentally required for, or is deepened by, single-variable equation solving at this same grade. Symmetric relatesTo therefore fits the bounded evidence better than a same-rank developmental direction. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), so absence of a stronger linking exemplar in the excerpts is not proof of absence.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 5 Indicators (same rank 1) in Strand 3 Geometry and Measurement but in different Sub-Strands: B5.3.1.1.2 uses paper folding of cut-out squares and rectangles to investigate side, angle and diagonal properties (Lines and Shapes), while B5.3.2.1.1 estimates perimeter with centimetre/metre referents, calculates actual perimeter of 2-D shapes and compares (Measurement). Their LCs ('investigate the properties of the sides of squares and rectangles' vs 'calculate the actual perimeter of 2-D shapes') show genuine conceptual coherence — knowledge of side properties of rectangles/squares reinforces work with the perimeter of those 2-D shapes — but the measurement indicator is framed around estimation, referents and unit measurement rather than derived from shape-property investigation, and same-rank placement offers no substantive directional evidence. Token/trigram and code-prefix overlap are negligible ('and', shared 'b5','3') and not themselves probative, so a symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment.

producer_judgment.rationale: Both are Indicator-grain statements at the same BASIC 6 coordinate (rank 2) under Content Standard B6.4.1.1 'Create, label, and interpret line graphs to draw conclusions' (Strand 4: Data). The second SFI (B6.4.1.1.1, LCs 'determine the common attributes (title, axes and intervals) of a line graph' and 'draw a line graph for a given table of values') establishes the constructive skill of building a line graph from tabulated values. The first SFI (B6.4.1.1.2, LCs 'determine whether a given set of data can be represented by a line graph (continuous data) or a series of points (discrete data)' and 'explain why') is a substantively more demanding judgement/justification task about representational appropriateness, which presupposes knowing how line graphs are structured and plotted. Since ranks are equal, direction rests on this pair-specific content escalation from construction to evaluative reasoning about continuous vs discrete data, so proficiency in the second supports success in the first. Evidence limitation: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and shared ancestry/code prefix alone was not treated as supporting evidence.
